Subject: MediPharma pilot — contracting & stakeholder orchestration

Tom / Sandra — thanks again for a focused conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop in legal/procurement: 

- Scope we agreed: 90-day inference pilot for two internal apps (clinical summarization + triage assistant); target start: mid-April.
- Success criteria: latency < 350ms p95 at 16k context, cost target ~ $0.004/token avg for productionized runs, and data-handling constraints for PHI redaction in logs.
- Key stakeholders you mentioned: Rajiv Patel (CFO / economic buyer), Sandra (Clinical lead), Procurement (procurement@medipharma.com) — confirm if I missed anyone.

Immediate asks/next steps: 
1) Procurement / Legal owners — can you confirm whether you prefer to sign a standalone mutual NDA first, or would you rather exchange an MSA/DPA with a redline pass? Either works for us but it changes turn times.
2) If NDA first: we’ll send our mutual NDA (attached). Typical turnaround we see from mid-market procurement is 3–5 business days for an initial signature; MSA redlines take longer.
3) If you want to route to specific contacts: please share the legal contact names and a primary procurement POC (email) so we can update the mutual action plan.

I attached a draft mutual NDA and a short contracting cheat-sheet that maps expected owner lanes and recommended sequencing on our side. Ben and Rachel looped for pricing and legal-ops coordination.

Thanks — I’ll be ready to schedule a quick 20-min sync with procurement/legal to walk through the agreement path if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Procurement prefers an NDA first (internal policy) before exchanging MSA templates. Can you send a clean mutual NDA we can circulate? We got your attachment but will run it through procurement/legal — fine if it’s a short doc.
- Estimated SLA/look-to-production obligations — procurement asked whether any data will leave our VPC. We heard PHI redaction mentioned; we need that explicitly stated in the DPA/MSA.

Thanks Tom — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and a proposed sequencing below.

Preferred sequencing (recommended to minimize delay):
A) Send mutual NDA (attached) to procurement@medipharma.com and legal@medipharma.com for signature (target turnaround: 2–4 business days).
B) While NDA is circulating, we’ll prep an MSA + DPA draft (internal Redwood template + short redline guidance) and share for a single-pass redline review. Expected on our side: first draft delivered within 3 business days after NDA signature.
C) Typical redline cycle: 1–2 substantive passes with procurement/legal; if you want, we can propose guardrail language for PHI/data residency clauses to speed review.

Owner lanes (our suggested):
- Procurement lane: procurement@medipharma.com (initial NDA routing + PO terms).
- Legal lane: legal@medipharma.com (MSA/DPA redlines).
- Commercial / Economic buyer: Rajiv Patel (final sign-off on spend). Ben will handle pricing & commercial terms in parallel.

Attachment: clean mutual NDA (v1) and an internal cheatsheet showing how we sequence NDA -> MSA -> DPA, plus recommended clause language for PHI handling.

If that sequencing looks good, I’ll route the NDA to procurement now and set a 30-minute legal walkthrough for Wednesday (Tues/Wed in your timezone) to talk through the DPA specifics.

Best,
Mina
